caption: Lightning flashes behind a lighthouse on a stormy coast, and the lighthouse is silhouetted while its own beam keeps sweeping.

sa.check: A lighthouse on a stormy coast.
The lighthouse stands as a dark silhouette against the flash.
The beam keeps sweeping through and after the flash.

pc.expect: The flash is brief: the sky behind the lighthouse brightens and returns to dark; flashes may repeat but each ends.
pc.fail: The sky stays lit for the rest of the clip; or brightens steadily; or the flash fades in slowly; or the sky turns to daylight.

pc.expect: The light comes from behind the lighthouse: the sky beyond it brightens while its near face stays dark; its own beam keeps sweeping at the same steady pace through the flash.
pc.fail: The near face of the lighthouse lights up while the sky behind stays dark; or the beam stops, jumps or reverses at the flash; or the beam goes out at the flash and returns afterwards; or the lighthouse glows brighter than the sky behind it.

pc.expect: The beam turns steadily about the lantern room in one direction, sweeping the sea and cloud.
pc.fail: The beam sweeps in one direction and then the other; or turns about a point other than the lantern; or two beams sweep in opposite directions from one lantern; or the beam bends.

pc.expect: The lighthouse, the rocks and the coastline are the same across dark and lit frames.
pc.fail: The lighthouse changes place or a second one appears; or rocks appear or vanish between frames; or the coastline changes shape; or the lantern room vanishes.

pc.expect: The lighthouse keeps its tower shape and stays solid; the flash does not pass through it or light it from within.
pc.fail: The tower becomes transparent with the flash seen through it; or the tower bends or changes shape; or a bolt emerges from the tower; or the tower merges with the rocks.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The tower's paint, the rocks and the sea keep their colours apart from the flash and the beam.
pc.fail: The tower changes colour or stripe pattern; or the sea changes colour permanently; or the sky changes colour permanently after the flash.
